exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Inverse of a Radical Function

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = -\dfrac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{x} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = -\dfrac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{y}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = -\dfrac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{y}\\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{y} & = -\dfrac{3}{2}x\\[5pt] (\sqrt[3]{y})^3 & = \left( -\dfrac{3}{2}x \right)^3\\[5pt] y & = -\dfrac{27}{8} x^3 \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = -\dfrac{27}{8} x^3. \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Radical Function

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{x} + 3 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{y} + 3. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{y} + 3\\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{y} & = x - 3\\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{y} & = 2(x - 3)\\[5pt] (\sqrt[3]{y})^3 & = \left( 2(x-3) \right)^3\\[5pt] y & = 8(x-3)^3 \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = 8(x-3)^3. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Inverse of a Reciprocal Radical Function

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{5}{2\sqrt[3]{x}} - 3.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac{5}{2\sqrt[3]{x}} -3 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac{5}{2\sqrt[3]{y}} -3. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac{5}{2\sqrt[3]{y}} -3 \\[5pt] \dfrac{5}{2\sqrt[3]{y}} & = x + 3\\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{y} &= \dfrac{5}{2(x+3)} \\[5pt] \left(\sqrt[3]{y}\right)^3 &= \left( \dfrac{5}{2(x+3)} \right)^3 \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{125}{8(x+3)^3} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) =\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{125}{8(x+3)^3}}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x \neq 0, \qquad f(x) \neq -3. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x \neq -3, \qquad f^{-1}(x) \neq 0. \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Reciprocal Radical Function

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = 5 - \dfrac{3}{8\sqrt{x}} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = 5 - \dfrac{3}{8\sqrt{y}}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = 5 - \dfrac{3}{8\sqrt{y}}\\[5pt] x - 5 & = -\dfrac{3}{8\sqrt{y}}\\[5pt] \sqrt{y} & = -\dfrac{3}{8(x-5)} \\[5pt] \big( \sqrt{y} \big)^2 &= \left( -\dfrac{3}{8(x-5)} \right)^2 \\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{9}{64(x-5)^2} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{9}{64(x-5)^2}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are given by \[ x > 0, \qquad f(x) \lt 5. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x \lt 5, \qquad f^{-1}(x) > 0. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Inverse of a Radical Function Containing a Linear Argument

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt[3]{2x - 3}} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt[3]{2y - 3}}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt[3]{2y - 3}}\\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{2y - 3} & = \dfrac{2}{x}\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt[3]{2y - 3} \right)^3 & = \left( \dfrac{2}{x} \right)^3\\[5pt] 2y - 3 & = \dfrac{8}{x^3}\\[5pt] 2y & = \dfrac{8}{x^3} + 3\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{4}{x^3} + \dfrac{3}{2} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{4}{x^3} + \dfrac{3}{2}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x \neq \dfrac{3}{2}, \qquad f(x) \neq 0. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x \neq 0, \qquad f^{-1}(x) \neq \dfrac{3}{2}. \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Radical Function Containing a Linear Argument

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \sqrt[3]{2x+3} - 4 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \sqrt[3]{2y+3} - 4. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \sqrt[3]{2y+3} - 4 \\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{2y+3} &= x + 4 \\[5pt] (\sqrt[3]{2y+3})^3 &= (x+4)^3 \\[5pt] 2y + 3 &= (x+4)^3 \\[5pt] 2y &= (x+4)^3 - 3 \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac12(x+4)^3 - \dfrac32 \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is

\[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac12(x+4)^3 - \dfrac32. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Determining an Unknown Value Given the Inverse of a Radical Function

question.text: The function $f(x) = 2 - \dfrac{1}{k} \sqrt[3]{2x + 4}$ has an inverse function given by $f^{-1}(x) = 32 (2 - x)^3 - 2.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = 2 - \dfrac{1}{k} \sqrt[3]{2x + 4} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = 2 - \dfrac{1}{k} \sqrt[3]{2 y + 4}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = 2 - \dfrac{1}{k} \sqrt[3]{2y + 4} \\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{k} \sqrt[3] {2y + 4} & = 2 - x \\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{2y + 4} & = k(2 - x )\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt[3]{2y + 4} \right)^3 & = \left( k (2 - x) \right)^3\\[5pt] 2y + 4 & = k^3 (2 - x)^3\\[5pt] 2y & = k^3 (2 - x)^3 - 4\\[5pt] y & =\dfrac {k^3} 2 (2 - x)^3 - 2 \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac {k^3} 2 (2 - x)^3 - 2. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that \[ \dfrac {k^3} 2 = 32 \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad k = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{4}. \]

example.title: Determining an Unknown Value Given the Inverse of a Radical Function

question.text:
The function $f(x),$ defined as \[ f(x) = \dfrac{2}{3\sqrt{x + k}} + 5,\qquad x \gt -k \] has an inverse function given by \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{4}{9(x-5)^2} - 2, \qquad x \gt 5. \]

What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac{2}{3\sqrt{x + k}} + 5 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac{2}{3\sqrt{y + k}} + 5. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac{2}{3\sqrt{y + k}} + 5\\[5pt] x - 5 & = \dfrac{2}{3\sqrt{y + k}}\\[5pt] \sqrt{y + k} & = \dfrac{2}{3(x-5)}\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt{y + k} \right)^2 & = \left( \dfrac{2}{3(x-5)} \right)^2 \\[5pt] y + k & = \dfrac{4}{9(x-5)^2}\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{4}{9(x-5)^2} - k \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is

\[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{4}{9(x-5)^2} - k, \qquad x \gt 5. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that \[ k = 2. \]
